subject: Re: Intermittent chunk starvation and elevated latency — OptiHealth (urgent)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@optihealth.com>

Cc: OptiHealth Platform <ops@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [urgent] Live responses freezing mid-stream (west-us)

Hi Rishi,

We're seeing a sharp degradation starting around 09:00 PT across several of our production users. Symptoms: streaming responses stop emitting tokens mid-chunk for ~5–30s, websocket connections from clients observe 408/499, p95 per-token response time has jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s, and our overall error-rate to the Redwood endpoints increased to ~4.2%. Throughput (requests/s) is down ~60% compared to baseline.

This is impacting our customer-facing recommender flows and execs are noticing. We captured session traces and a metric dump (attached: optihealth-telemetry-20270614.json, opti_session_trace.har). All traffic is to the hosted us-west endpoint with the standard streaming client (ws, chunked transfer).

Can you please triage urgently and let us know immediate mitigations (routing or config) we can apply? We have a 1pm PT call on standby.

Thanks,
Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, OptiHealth
ops@optihealth.com

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: [urgent] Live responses freezing mid-stream (west-us)

Thanks — initial engineering findings below (preliminary):

Summary: between 09:00–09:07 PT we observed a correlated increase in edge-proxy websocket keepalive timeouts and a backlog of small chunk buffers in the core proxy layer. The core runtime still generated tokens (CPU/GPU utilization normal) but the proxy wasn't flushing those chunks to the socket immediately — they were coalesced and delayed. When client churn increased, TCP write buffers filled and some sockets stalled, leading to client-side 408/499 and apparent "mid-chunk" silence.

Key metrics (west-us cluster):
- Keepalive timeout rate: baseline 0.02% -> spike 3.8% at 09:03
- Token flush latency (proxy to socket): p50 85ms -> p95 2.1s
- Error rate to your account: 0.6% -> 4.2%
- Throughput (tokens/s) for account: -58% relative drop

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a recent kernel/epoll tweak we rolled two nights ago changed epoll behavior under specific socket reuse patterns; downstream proxy started coalescing and delaying chunk flushes under certain churn patterns. The net effect: tokens generated were queued but not pushed to the client promptly.

Immediate mitigations (we're pushing now):
1) Increase websocket keepalive (edge) to 45s for OptiHealth account — in progress (applied at 10:06).
2) Disable HTTP/1.1 chunk coalescing on the proxy for your traffic — hotfix deployed to a canary pool at 10:12.
3) Warm handoff: route OptiHealth traffic to a dedicated pool (no shared proxy instance) — initiated, should finish within 18m.

Attached: sample trace IDs (optisession-3e2a, optisession-7c9b), small log snippet:
[2027-06-14T09:03:12Z] proxy.write_queue_len=152 -> socket.write returned EAGAIN
[2027-06-14T09:03:13Z] edge.keepalive_timeout inc 0.04% -> 3.8%
[2027-06-14T09:04:01Z] client 35.191.22.14 closed ws with 499

We'll continue to monitor and report back. If this stabilizes after the routing change we'll follow with a postmortem describing the kernel/epoll interaction and longer-term fix.

-Grace

Engineering has applied a canary hotfix (disable chunk coalescing) and started routing to a dedicated pool. Early signals: partial stabilization but residual p95 token latency still elevated (~600ms) for a subset of sessions. Customer execs are on the 13:00 call and asked for leadership visibility.

Please prioritize:

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [resolved] Root cause and remediation for OptiHealth streaming stalls

Update — final write-up and resolution steps:

Root cause: an interaction between a recent kernel/epoll tweak (rolled 2027-06-12) and our proxy socket reuse pattern caused the proxy to coalesce small chunk writes and delay flushes under particular churn and buffer-fill scenarios. That, combined with client churn, resulted in transient TCP write buffer saturation and websocket stalls.

What we changed:
- Hotfix deployed (Europe/US canaries, then all) to disable chunk coalescing on the proxy for streaming paths (deployed 2027-06-14 10:12 PT).
- Increased websocket keepalive at edge for OptiHealth to 45s (10:06 PT).
- Failed over OptiHealth traffic to a dedicated pool to remove noisy neighbor effects (10:28 PT).
- Reverted the small epoll behavior change in the proxy stack; working with infra to submit kernel compatibility patches for staging.

Customer impact: stabilization observed within 20 minutes of routing change; p95 token latency returned to ~150–220ms by 10:40 PT; error-rate reduced to <0.5% for OptiHealth. No data loss observed.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem doc (JIRA-INF-5423) being drafted — timeline target EOD tomorrow.
2) Regression tests added to ci/integration to catch the epoll+proxy pattern under churn.
3) Offer SLA credit options to OptiHealth via Marissa (CS).

Attachments: optihealth-telemetry-20270614.json, opti_support_screenshot.png, opti_session_trace.har

If you want the technical deep-dive I'll drop the full trace and packet captures to the JIRA ticket.

- Dev
